text:
Linus: quick sync — I put together a short proposal for a strict apples-to-apples compare between model variants. goal: remove all infra/decoder/tokenizer differences so we can blame kernels/batching/KV only.

Joyce: +1. can you list the invariants we'll lock? also want to ensure replay harness vs synthetic traffic is explicit.

Linus: proposed invariants: same prompt set, identical tokenization (shared tokenizer binary + config), identical decoding params (temp, top_p, stop sequences), same KV warmup strategy, identical batching policy (batch size distribution), and pinned hardware/driver versions.

Ben: for replay vs synth: replay = real traces from prod sanitized; synth = controlled load generator that matches seq-len and concurrency distribution. we should run both. replay to validate realism, synth to stress kernel heuristics deterministically.

Asha: +1. Kernel selection note: we must pin kernel selector config file and log chosen kernel for each call. otherwise v2 vs v1 selection differences confound results. add a column in results for chosen kernel id.

Linus: agreed. also want to capture KV cache hit-rate + first-token latency vs warmed state. plan: two passes per model: cold-start (no KV) and warmed (replay with same prefixes to pre-populate KV).

Joyce: sounds good. for tokenizer alignment — can we use the CLI to ensure identical token counts? suggestion: run `tokenize-check --model <m> --prompts prompts.json` and assert token_count == canonical_tokens.json.

Matt: sample run command for replay harness (for clarity):
```
./harness/replay --trace traces/2025-08-02.json \
  --model-id redwood/open-350M-v1 \
  --decode 'temp=0.0,top_p=0.95,stop=["\n\n"]' \
  --pin-kernel-config configs/kernel-lock.json \
  --batch-policy configs/batch-uniform.json \
  --kv-warmup prefill-prefixes.json
```

Ben: perf-regression note from last run: when we switched the kernel selector to prefer tiled-matmul-v2, p50 looked fine but p95 regressed ~12% on short prompts (<32 tok). suspect tiling overhead on tiny sequences.

Asha: got a short profiler snippet (sampled):
```
flame: tiled_matmul: 54%
flame: memcpy: 18%
flame: decode-loop: 12%
```
I'll attach full flamegraphs to the ticket.

Linus: let's record exact decoder params in a metadata file per run (json) and store alongside traces. if anyone changes batch heuristic or kernel selector we must re-run the whole compare.

Joyce: acceptance criteria for the compare:
- tokenizer counts match for all prompts
- decode outputs are bit-compatible for greedy runs (temp=0) up to stop sequence boundary
- latency/throughput table with kernels/batching configs side-by-side
- KV cold vs warm delta reported separately

Ben: also capture per-request chosen kernel id, batch size, seq-len, kv-hit bool. those are critical for slicing.

Matt: bench-bot run summary (latest synthetic sweep):
```
bench-bot: sweep finished 1954323000
models: open-350M-v1, opt-350M-quant
p95 latency (open-350M-v1): 82ms (synth), 75ms (replay)
p95 latency (open-350M-v1) tiled-matmul-v2: 92ms (synth) -> +12%
kv-warm: reduces p95 by 18% on avg for >64 token flows
```

Asha: interesting that replay p95 is lower than synth for that model — implies our synthetic load may over-index on very short bursts. we should tune the load generator to match seq-len histogram from traces.

Linus: action items:
1) Joyce/Matt: finalize canonical prompt set + tokenizer binary (due EOD Thursday)
2) Ben: run full replay sweep with kernel logging + KV cold/warm (due Fri)
3) Asha: generate flamegraphs for tiled-matmul-v2 regression and try small-tile fallback (due Fri)
4) bench-bot: store per-run metadata in s3://redwood-bench/runs/<thread_ts>/metadata.json

Joyce: @Ben can you also make the harness assert token counts and fail fast if mismatch? would save time.

Ben: will add assert. also adding a `--strict-kernel-lock` flag to ensure config violations fail.

Linus: awesome. once we have run results, we'll produce a short apples-to-apples writeup with tables and flamegraphs. keep logs short and include sample traces for reproducibility. :thumbsup:

bench-bot: noted actions scheduled. run artifacts will be linked as they complete.
